pois.name: Albert Park Tunnels
pois.intro: The Albert Park tunnels are found largely beneath Albert Park, in central Auckland, New Zealand. The tunnels were constructed as air raid shelters during the Second World War.

pois.name: New Zealand Maritime Museum Hui Te Ananui a Tangaroa
pois.intro: The New Zealand Maritime Museum Hui Te Ananui a Tangaroa is a maritime museum in Auckland, New Zealand. It is located on Hobson Wharf, adjacent to the Viaduct Harbour in central Auckland.

pois.name: Toi o Tāmaki / Auckland Art Gallery
pois.wikipedia: en:Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
pois.intro: Auckland Art Gallery is the principal public gallery in Auckland, New Zealand. It has the most extensive collection of national and international art in New Zealand and frequently hosts travelling international exhibitions.

pois.name: Sky Tower
pois.intro: The Sky Tower is a telecommunications and observation tower in Auckland, New Zealand.

pois.name: Y turret of HMNZS Achilles
pois.intro: HMNZS Achilles was a Leander-class light cruiser, the second of five in the class. She served in the Royal New Zealand Navy in the Second World War.

pois.name: Tāmaki Paenga Hira / Auckland War Memorial Museum
pois.intro: The Auckland War Memorial Museum, also known as Auckland Museum, is one of New Zealand's most important museums and war memorials. Its neoclassical building constructed in the 1920s and 1950s, stands on Observatory Hill, the remains of a dormant volcano, in the Auckland Domain, near Auckland CBD. Museum collections concentrate on New Zealand history, natural history, and military history.

pois.name: Maungakiekie / One Tree Hill
pois.intro: Maungakiekie / One Tree Hill is a 182-metre volcanic peak and Tūpuna Maunga in Auckland, New Zealand. It is an important place culturally and archeologically for both Māori and Pākehā.

pois.name: Auckland Zoo
pois.intro: Auckland Zoo is a 16.35-hectare not-for-profit wildlife conservation organisation that focuses on the wellbeing of people, wildlife and nature. The zoo is located in Auckland, New Zealand, specificly next to Te Waiōrea Western Springs Park.

pois.name: Emirates Team New Zealand Base
pois.description:
used by Ineos Team UK 2019-2022
used by Emirates Team NZ 2022-2028
pois.intro: Team New Zealand or TNZ is a sailing team based in Auckland, New Zealand, representing the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron. The team has been branded as Emirates Team New Zealand at America's Cup competitions since 2007.

pois.name: Pukekawa / Auckland Domain
pois.intro: The Auckland Domain, also known as Pukekawa / Auckland Domain, is a large park in Auckland, New Zealand. Consisting of 75 hectares of land, Auckland Domain is the oldest park in the city.

pois.name: SEA LIFE Kelly Tarlton's Aquarium
pois.intro: Kelly Tarlton's Sea Life Aquarium is a public aquarium opened on 25 January 1985 in Auckland, New Zealand. Located at 23 Tamaki Drive, it was the brainchild of New Zealand marine archaeologist and diver Kelly Tarlton.

pois.name: KZ1 Yacht
pois.intro: KZ1, formally called the New Zealand, is a one-off sailing yacht built to challenge for the 1988 America's Cup. She was designed by Bruce Farr and is constructed from a carbon fibre and Kevlar/Nomex sandwich, skippered by David Barnes and crewed by a team of 40 from the Mercury Bay Boating Club in Whitianga, New Zealand.

pois.name: Aotea Square
pois.intro: Aotea Square is a large paved public area in the CBD of Auckland, New Zealand. Officially opened in 1979 by Sir Dove-Myer Robinson next to Queen Street, it is used for open-air concerts and gatherings, markets, and political rallies.

pois.name: Maungawhau / Mount Eden
pois.intro: Maungawhau / Mount Eden is a scoria cone and Tūpuna Maunga in Mount Eden, Auckland, New Zealand. The cone is part of the Auckland volcanic field, the tallest located on the isthmus.

pois.name: Freyberg Field
pois.intro: Kiwitea Street, also known as Freyberg Field, is a multi-purpose stadium in the suburb of Sandringham in Auckland, New Zealand. It is used for Association football matches and is the home stadium of both Auckland City FC and Central United.

pois.name: Ōwairaka / Te Ahi-kā-a-Rakataura / Mount Albert
pois.intro: Ōwairaka / Mount Albert, also known as Te Ahi-kā-a-Rakataura, is a volcanic peak and Tūpuna Maunga which dominates the landscape of the Ōwairaka and Mount Albert suburbs of Auckland.

pois.name: Te Kōpuke / Tītīkōpuke / Mount Saint John
pois.intro: Mount Saint John, is a volcanic scoria cone and Tūpuna Maunga in Epsom, in the Auckland volcanic field of New Zealand.

pois.name: Maungarei / Mount Wellington
pois.intro: Maungarei / Mount Wellington is a 135-metre volcanic peak and Tūpuna Maunga located in the Auckland volcanic field of Auckland, New Zealand. It is the youngest onshore volcano of the Auckland volcanic field, having been formed by an eruption around 10,000 years ago.

pois.name: Gus Fisher
pois.intro: Gus Fisher Gallery is a contemporary art gallery owned and operated by the University of Auckland in Auckland, New Zealand. It is located in the Kenneth Myers Centre, a historic building restored in 2000 with the help of the gallery's patron, Gus Fisher.

pois.name: Gow Langsford Gallery
pois.intro: Gow Langsford Gallery is a commercial art gallery in Auckland, New Zealand. The gallery was established in 1987 by John Gow and Gary Langsford.

pois.name: Tautai Pacific Arts Trust
pois.intro: Tautai Pacific Arts Trust, also known as Tautai, is a Pacific gallery in Auckland, New Zealand and a charitable trust founded by Fatu Feu'u to empower Pacific arts in New Zealand. The gallery is described as 'a first-of-its-kind Pacific gallery in central Auckland' by Radio New Zealand.

pois.name: Artspace
pois.intro: Artspace Aotearoa is an art gallery in Auckland, New Zealand. It is located on Karangahape Road in Newton.

pois.name: Maota Sāmoa / Sāmoa House
pois.intro: Samoa House, also known as Maota Samoa, is a building at 283 Karangahape Road in Auckland, New Zealand. The first fale outside of Samoa, it was built using funds raised by the Samoa House Appeal Fund, and opened on 15 December 1978.

pois.name: Bluestone Store
pois.intro: The Bluestone Store is a warehouse building in the Auckland City Centre of New Zealand. Built in 1861, the warehouse operated as the Bluestone Room, a pub and restaurant, from 2003 until 2020.

pois.name: National Museum of the Royal New Zealand Navy
pois.nameEnglish: National Museum of the Royal New Zealand Navy

pois.name: Bean Rock
pois.description: FR on One Tree Hill 4.7M SW
pois.intro: Bean Rock Lighthouse is a lighthouse situated at the end of a reef in the Waitematā Harbour in Auckland, New Zealand. It is the only remaining example in New Zealand of a wooden cottage-style lighthouse, and it is one of only a few remaining worldwide.

pois.name: General Assembly House
pois.intro: The General Assembly House, colloquially called "Shedifice" by the members of Parliament, was the first building to house the New Zealand Parliament in Auckland. It was in use by Parliament from 1854 until 1864 during the time that Auckland was the capital of New Zealand.

pois.name: Highwic
pois.intro: Highwic is a 19th-century house in Auckland, New Zealand, which is listed by Heritage New Zealand as a Category I structure. The house was built in 1862 for Alfred Buckland, a wealthy colonial settler and landowner.

pois.name: Albert Park
pois.intro: Albert Park is a public park in central Auckland, bounded by Wellesley Street East, Princes Street, Bowen Avenue and Kitchener Street. From the entrance at the corner of Bowen Ave and Kitchener St, sealed footpaths climb steeply through a variety of trees to the large flat area at the summit, where a formal layout of paths and flower gardens encircle a fountain.

pois.name: Maungawhau / Mount Eden
pois.intro: Maungawhau / Mount Eden is a scoria cone and Tūpuna Maunga in Mount Eden, Auckland, New Zealand. The cone is part of the Auckland volcanic field, the tallest located on the isthmus.

pois.name: Tuff Crater Reserve
pois.intro: Tank Farm is the name of a volcanic explosion crater on the North Shore of Auckland, New Zealand, near the approaches to the Auckland Harbour Bridge.

pois.name: Waiatarau / Victoria Park
pois.intro: Victoria Park is a park and sports ground in the Auckland city centre, New Zealand. It was opened in 1905 and named after the queen who had died four years earlier.

pois.name: Myers Park
pois.intro: Myers Park is a narrow park in central Auckland, New Zealand, running parallel to the upper part of Queen Street. It is characterised by steep, grassed slopes and canopied with a mixture of large exotic and native trees, including an alley of large palm trees.

pois.name: Parnell Rose Garden
pois.intro: Dove-Myer Robinson Park, more commonly known as the Parnell Rose Garden, is a park in Parnell, Auckland, New Zealand. The park is named after Dove-Myer Robinson, the longest-serving mayor of Auckland, who served for 18 years.
